description: Autotest Request issues that the Claude Implement Autotests workflow is measured on. Each was closed by a bot pull request that a maintainer finished and merged, and the spec at `base` is the reference. Before generation the run deletes the `reference.remove` paths (the spec, its snapshots and its test-data folder), so the model cannot copy the reference. `body` is the issue text as the prompt gets it.

entries.title: Autotests: Introducing rotation of monomers in Macromolecules mode
entries.body:
**Source task(s):**
 - https://github.com/epam/ketcher/issues/8352

- [x] Verify that rotation is enabled in Macromolecules mode when two monomers without any bonds between them are selected
- [ ] Verify that rotation is enabled in Macromolecules mode when two monomers with bonds between them are selected
- [ ] Verify that rotation is enabled in Macromolecules mode when more than two monomers are selected, regardless of whether they are connected by bonds
- [ ] Verify that rotation is not enabled in Macromolecules mode when only one monomer is selected
- [ ] Verify that a bounding box with a rotaition handle and a cross in the center of rotation appears when two or more monomers are selected in Macromolecules mode
- [ ] Verify that there are rotation, flip, delete buttons above the bounding box for selected monomers in Macromolecules mode 
- [ ] Verify that in Macromolecules mode rotation angles are displayed near the bounding box while rotating
- [ ] Verify that the default rotation angle is set to 15° in Macromolecules mode
- [ ] Verify that rotation mode gets activated in Macromolecules mode by pressing the left mouse button (a rotation handle turns blue, a cross turns blue, and a blue dashed line connectes them, the bounding box is replaced with a circle)
- [ ] Verify that when rotation mode is deactivated in Macromolecules mode, the selected fragment remains in its new position, rotation circle is replaced with the bounding box, that is redrawn at its initial position, and all labels of the rotated fragment are aligned with horizontal axis
- [ ] Verify that 'flip horizontally', 'flip vertically' and 'delete' buttons work as expected in Macromolecule mode
- [ ] Verify that when rotation mode is activated, the center of the circle is at the center of rotation, the circle's diameter is equal to the height of the replaced bounding box
- [ ] Verify that when rotation mode is activated in Macromolecule mode the following predefined angles is marked on the rotation circle: -90, -60, -45, -30, 0, 30, 45, 60, 90
- [ ] Verify that when rotation starts in Macromolecule mode, the set of angles shown always covers the range [-90 - +90] relatively to the handle position
- [ ] Verify that when rotation starts in Macromolecule mode, the current rotation angle is displayed at starting position
- [ ] Verify ability to move the center of rotation in Macromolecules mode

entries.title: Autotests: Defining the preset - presets in the monomer creation wizard
entries.body:
**Source task(s):**
- https://github.com/epam/ketcher/issues/8854

- [ ] Verify preset primary field is labeled 'Code' instead of 'Name' on preset definition tab
-- 1. Open Monomer Creation Wizard.
-- 2. Create or edit a preset (e.g., type 'Nucleotide (preset)').
-- 3. Navigate to the tab/section where preset main identifier is entered.
-- 4. Inspect the label of the primary text field at the top of the preset section.
-- Expected result: The primary preset identifier field is labeled 'Code' (not 'Name'); the field position and basic behavior remain as before (no logic change).
- [ ] Verify preset code is mandatory and triggers 'Mandatory fields must be filled.' when empty on save
-- 1. Open Monomer Creation Wizard and switch to preset creation flow.
-- 2. Leave the 'Code' field completely empty.
-- 3. Fill in all other required fields for saving a preset (e.g., components, any other mandatory properties).
-- 4. Click 'Save' / 'Finish' in the wizard.
-- Expected result: Saving is blocked. An error message appears: 'Mandatory fields must be filled.' The Code field and the preset tab are highlighted in red until a non-empty value is entered.
- [ ] Verify preset code must be unique amongst other preset codes
-- 1. Create and save a preset with Code value 'PRESET1'.
-- 2. Open the wizard again to create a second preset.
-- 3. Enter Code 'PRESET1' for the new preset.
-- 4. Fill in all other required fields.
-- 5. Attempt to save the second preset.
-- Expected result: Saving the second preset is blocked. Error message appears: 'The preset code must be unique amongst other presets.' The Code field and preset tab are highlighted in red until a different unique code is entered.
- [ ] Verify allowed characters in preset code (letters, digits, hyphens, underscores, asterisks) are accepted
-- 1. Open the preset creation wizard.
-- 2. In the Code field, enter a value using only allowed characters, e.g. 'AbC-12_*', 'abc', 'ABC123', 'CODE-1', 'CODE_2', 'CODE*3'.
-- 3. Ensure all other required fields are valid.
-- 4. Attempt to save the preset for several examples of valid codes.
-- Expected result: "Presets with codes containing only uppercase/lowercase letters, numbers, hyphens (-), underscores (_), and asterisks (*) save successfully. No validation error is shown for these codes, and no red highlighting appears.
- [ ] Verify invalid characters in preset code trigger specific validation error message
-- 1. Open the preset creation wizard.
-- 2. In the Code field, enter a value with at least one invalid character, e.g. 'PRE SET', 'PRESET#1', 'PRESET@1', 'PRESET+1'.
-- 3. Ensure other required fields are valid.
-- 4. Attempt to save the preset.
-- Expected result: Saving is blocked. Error message appears exactly as defined: 'The preset code must consist only of uppercase and lowercase letters, numbers, hyphens (`-`), underscores (`_`), and asterisks (`*`).' The Code field and preset tab are highlighted in red until the invalid characters are removed.
- [ ] Verify error highlighting on Code field and preset tab is cleared after fixing issues
-- 1. Trigger a validation error for the Code field (e.g. leave it empty or use an invalid character) and attempt to save.
-- 2. Confirm that the Code field and preset tab are highlighted in red.
-- 3. Edit the Code field to a valid, unique value using only allowed characters.
-- 4. Attempt to save again.
-- Expected result: On the first attempt, errors and red highlighting appear. After correcting the Code and saving successfully, the Code field and preset tab no longer have red highlighting. No further validation error for Code is shown.
- [ ] Verify monomer codes auto-update when preset code changes for auto-generated monomer codes
-- 1. Create a new preset with Code 'ABC'.
-- 2. Allow the wizard to auto-generate monomer codes for components (e.g. Base, Sugar, Phosphate) using the preset code.
-- 3. Confirm the initial monomer codes follow the expected default pattern (e.g. 'ABCB', 'ABCS', 'ABCP' or analogous as defined in previous ticket).
-- 4. Change the preset Code to 'XYZ'.
-- 5. Observe monomer codes for components that were not manually edited.
-- Expected result: For all components whose monomer codes are still in default/auto-generated state, their codes are updated to reflect the new preset Code (e.g. from 'ABCB' to 'XYZB', etc.). The update is applied immediately when the preset Code changes or at the next validation step, as designed.
- [ ] Verify manually changed monomer code is not auto-updated when preset code changes
-- 1. Create a new preset with Code 'ABC'.
-- 2. Confirm auto-generated monomer codes for all components.
-- 3. Manually change one monomer code (e.g. Base code) to a custom value such as 'BASE_CUSTOM'.
-- 4. Change the preset Code to a new value (e.g. 'XYZ').
-- 5. Inspect all monomer codes in the wizard.
-- Expected result: Monomer codes for components that remain in their default state update to reflect the new preset Code. The manually edited monomer code (e.g. 'BASE_CUSTOM') remains unchanged and is not overwritten by the preset Code change.
- [ ] Verify multiple sequential changes of preset code keep auto-update logic consistent
-- 1. Create a preset with Code 'AAA' and auto-generated monomer codes.
-- 2. Change Code to 'BBB' and verify non-overridden monomer codes update accordingly.
-- 3. Change Code again to 'CCC'.
-- 4. Inspect monomer codes after each change.
-- Expected result: After each change of the preset Code, all monomer codes that have not been manually changed are updated to use the latest preset Code value. Any monomer codes manually overridden at any step remain unchanged throughout subsequent preset Code changes.
- [ ] Verify existing presets with valid codes still save successfully after introducing new validation rules
-- 1. Open an existing preset created before this change that has a valid Code according to the new rules.
-- 2. Open it in the wizard without changing the Code.
-- 3. Click 'Save' / 'Finish'.
-- Expected result: Existing presets with already valid codes save successfully without triggering new validation errors. No unexpected errors appear solely due to the introduction of the new preset-Code validation logic.
- [ ] Verify IDT and AxoLabs aliases for presets follow same uniqueness and validation rules as for monomers
-- 1. Identify or create two presets using IDT/AxoLabs alias fields (if present in the preset wizard).
-- 2. For the first preset, set IDT and/or AxoLabs alias values according to valid monomer rules.
-- 3. Attempt to create a second preset with the same alias values that would violate monomer-level uniqueness.
-- 4. Attempt to save the second preset.
-- Expected result: Behavior of IDT and AxoLabs alias fields for presets matches the existing monomer behavior (same allowed characters and uniqueness rules). If aliases must be unique, saving the second preset is blocked with the same style of error and highlighting used for monomers.

entries.title: Autotests: Monomer saving - presets in the monomer creation wizard
entries.body:
**Source task(s):**
 - https://github.com/epam/ketcher/issues/8857

- [x] Verify that all monomers composing a preset are saved as hidden entries in the monomer library
-- 1. Open Monomer Creation Wizard and select 'Nucleotide (preset)'.
-- 2. Define Base, Sugar, and Phosphate components so that all three are created as new monomers (do not reuse existing monomers from the library).
-- 3. Complete all required preset fields and click 'Finish' / 'Save' to successfully create the preset.
-- 4. Open the Monomer Library.
-- 5. Search for the auto-generated monomer codes/names for Base, Sugar, and Phosphate.
-- 6. Optionally export monomer data (or use developer tools) to verify internal storage.
-- Expected result: All three component monomers (Base, Sugar, Phosphate) are saved internally but do not appear as visible entries in the Monomer Library UI (they are 'hidden'). Internally, the hidden monomers exist and are associated with the preset, but the user cannot see or select them directly from the library.
- [x] Verify that presets composed only of existing visible monomers do not create additional visible monomer entries
-- 1. Ensure there are already some visible monomers in the library for Base, Sugar, and Phosphate.
-- 2. Open the preset wizard and create a preset that reuses these existing monomers as its components (select them where possible instead of creating new ones).
-- 3. Save the preset successfully.
-- 4. Open the Monomer Library and compare the list of monomers before and after creating the preset.
-- Expected result: No new visible monomer entries are created in the library as a result of saving the preset when all components reuse existing monomers. The preset itself becomes available where presets are listed; the monomer library content remains unchanged.
- [x] Verify that hidden monomer properties are not checked for uniqueness against visible monomers
-- 1. Identify a visible monomer in the library with a specific code and name (e.g., Base code 'B1').
-- 2. Open the preset wizard and define a new preset where one component (e.g., Base) is created as a new monomer with the SAME code and name as the existing visible monomer.
-- 3. Ensure that this new component will be saved as a hidden monomer (do not explicitly add it to the library as a standalone monomer).
-- 4. Complete the preset and click 'Finish' / 'Save'.
-- Expected result: Saving the preset succeeds. No uniqueness error is raised for the hidden monomer even though its code/name duplicate an existing visible monomer. The hidden monomer is stored internally for the preset, while the visible monomer remains unchanged.
- [x] Verify that hidden monomer properties are not checked for uniqueness across different presets
-- 1. Create and save Preset A that generates hidden monomers with specific codes/names (e.g., Base='HB1', Sugar='HS1', Phosphate='HP1').
-- 2. Create Preset B in the wizard and define new components that will again be saved as hidden monomers.
-- 3. In Preset B, set the component codes/names to the same values as in Preset A (HB1, HS1, HP1) so that hidden monomers would conflict if uniqueness were enforced.
-- 4. Complete Preset B and save it.
-- 5. Observe any validation or error behavior.
-- Expected result: Preset B saves successfully with no uniqueness errors raised for hidden monomer properties. Both presets may internally have hidden monomers with the same codes/names without violating uniqueness constraints.
- [x] Verify that hidden monomer properties are still validated for formatting (invalid characters block preset saving)
-- 1. Open the preset creation wizard and define at least one component that will be saved as a new hidden monomer (e.g., Base).
-- 2. In the component properties (e.g., Base code), enter a value with invalid characters according to monomer formatting rules (e.g., include spaces or disallowed symbols such as '#', '@').
-- 3. Complete other fields so that all requirements are satisfied except the invalid formatting.
-- 4. Click 'Finish' / 'Save'.
-- Expected result: Saving the preset is blocked. A formatting validation error is shown for the affected hidden monomer field (e.g., code), using the same message and style as for visible monomers. The hidden monomer must satisfy formatting rules even though uniqueness is not enforced.
- [x] Verify that fixing formatting issues for hidden monomer properties allows preset to be saved
-- 1. From the previous scenario, with a formatting error on a hidden monomer property, correct the value (e.g., change the code to use only allowed characters).
-- 2. Ensure all other required fields are valid.
-- 3. Click 'Finish' / 'Save' again.
-- 4. Observe error state and saving behavior.
-- Expected result: "After correcting the formatting, the preset is saved successfully. No new uniqueness checks are applied to the hidden monomer, and no further errors are shown for the corrected property.
- [x] Verify that visible monomer creation still enforces uniqueness while hidden monomers do not
-- 1. Create a visible monomer via the standard monomer creation flow with a unique code/name (e.g., 'VISIBLE1').
-- 2. Attempt to create another visible monomer with the exact same code/name using the same flow.
-- 3. Observe that uniqueness validation triggers and blocks the second visible monomer.
-- 4. Now open the preset wizard and create a preset that defines a hidden monomer with code/name 'VISIBLE1'.
-- 5. Save the preset.
-- Expected result: Step 2–3: Uniqueness validation correctly prevents creating a second visible monomer with duplicate code/name. Step 4–5: The preset with a hidden monomer using the same code/name 'VISIBLE1' saves successfully, demonstrating that hidden monomers are exempt from uniqueness checks while visible monomers are not.
- [x] Verify that hidden monomers created with a preset are not selectable as components when creating other presets
-- 1. Create a preset that generates new hidden monomers for Base, Sugar, and Phosphate.
-- 2. Save the preset.
-- 3. Open the preset wizard again to create a second preset.
-- 4. In the component selection UI (if it allows choosing from existing monomers), attempt to search for and select the hidden monomers created in step 1.
-- 5. Observe the available options.
-- Expected result: Hidden monomers created by the first preset do not appear in the list of selectable monomers when defining components for a new preset. Only visible monomers are available for explicit reuse; hidden monomers remain internal and non-selectable.

entries.title: Autotests: Exiting the wizard - presets in the monomer creation wizard
entries.body:
**Source task(s):**
 - https://github.com/epam/ketcher/issues/8464

- [x] Verify success message text when creating a new preset via monomer creation wizard
-- 1. Open Monomer Creation Wizard.
-- 2. In the type dropdown, select 'Nucleotide (preset)' (or any preset type that uses the preset wizard).
-- 3. Fill in all required fields for the preset (components, properties, preset code, etc.).
-- 4. Click 'Finish' / 'Save' to successfully exit the wizard.
-- 5. Observe the confirmation message shown after the wizard closes.
-- Expected result: A confirmation toast/dialog appears with the exact text: 'The preset was successfully added to the library'. The old message 'The monomer was successfully added to the library.' is not shown in this flow.
- [x] Verify success message text when creating a preset from an alternative entry point into the wizard
-- 1. Open the Monomer Library panel.
-- 2. Use an alternative entry point to start preset creation (for example: 'Add preset' button or context menu, depending on implementation).
-- 3. Ensure 'Nucleotide (preset)' flow is used.
-- 4. Fill in all mandatory preset fields.
-- 5. Click 'Finish' / 'Save' and exit the wizard.
-- 6. Observe the confirmation message.
-- Expected result: Regardless of how the preset creation wizard was opened, after a successful save the confirmation text is exactly: 'The preset was successfully added to the library'.
- [x] Verify canceling preset creation does not show success message
-- 1. Open Monomer Creation Wizard and select 'Nucleotide (preset)'.
-- 2. Optionally enter some data in the wizard.
-- 3. Click 'Cancel' or close the wizard using the standard cancel/close action.
-- 4. Observe notifications and messages after the wizard closes.
-- Expected result: The preset is not saved. No success confirmation message ('The preset was successfully added to the library') is shown after canceling.
- [x] Verify validation errors prevent showing preset success message
-- 1. Open the preset creation wizard.
-- 2. Leave at least one required field invalid or empty (for example, Code field empty).
-- 3. Click 'Finish' / 'Save'.
-- 4. Observe wizard behavior and messages.
-- 5. Fix all validation errors and save again successfully.
-- Expected result: On the first attempt, the wizard stays open and shows validation errors; no success message about the preset being added to the library appears. Only after all errors are fixed and the save succeeds is the message 'The preset was successfully added to the library' displayed.
- [x] Verify non-preset monomer creation still uses monomer-specific success message
-- 1. Open Monomer Creation Wizard.
-- 2. Select a non-preset monomer type (e.g., 'Nucleotide (monomer)' or 'Small molecule').
-- 3. Fill in all required fields.
-- 4. Click 'Finish' / 'Save'.
-- 5. Observe the confirmation message.
-- Expected result: The success message for non-preset monomer creation remains unchanged and mentions 'monomer' (e.g., 'The monomer was successfully added to the library.'), confirming preset changes did not impact non-preset flows.
- [x] Verify success message is not duplicated for a single successful preset save
-- 1. Open the preset creation wizard and create a valid preset.
-- 2. Click 'Finish' / 'Save'.
-- 3. Observe the confirmation message behavior.
-- 4. Confirm that the message appears once and follows standard auto-hide/dismiss behavior.
-- Expected result: Exactly one confirmation message with text 'The preset was successfully added to the library' is shown per successful save action. No duplicate or repeated identical success messages appear for the same event.
- [x] Verify success message appears after preset creation in environments with different UI shells (e.g., standalone vs embedded)
-- 1. Run Ketcher in standalone mode (or primary deployment environment).
-- 2. Create a new preset via the wizard and save it; observe the success message.
-- 3. Run Ketcher in an embedded/integrated environment (if applicable, e.g., embedded in a host application).
-- 4. Create a new preset via the wizard and save it.
-- 5. Observe the success message in the embedded scenario.
-- Expected result: In each supported deployment environment, after successfully saving a preset the same confirmation text 'The preset was successfully added to the library' is displayed. Message delivery mechanism is consistent across environments (toast, dialog, etc., according to UX).

entries.title: Autotests: Defining other monomer properties - presets in the monomer creation wizard
entries.body:
**Source task(s):**
 - https://github.com/epam/ketcher/issues/8775

- [x] Verify ability to leave component properties undefined in monomer wizard
-- 1. Open Monomer Creation Wizard
-- 2. Select any preset type
-- 3. Proceed to 'Other monomer properties'
-- 4. Leave all fields empty except structure
-- 5. Click Next and Finish
-- Expected result: Wizard allows progression and preset creation without validation errors
- [x] Verify fully defined base is saved as visible monomer
-- 1. Open wizard
-- 2. Define base structure
-- 3. Fill all required properties
-- 4. Leave sugar and phosphate empty
-- 5. Create preset
-- Expected result: Preset created; base appears in Monomer Library as visible item
- [x] Verify fully defined sugar is saved as visible monomer
-- 1. Define sugar fully
-- 2. Leave base/phosphate undefined
-- 3. Create preset
-- Expected result: Sugar becomes visible in library
- [x] Verify fully defined phosphate is saved as visible monomer
-- 1. Define phosphate fully
-- 2. Leave other components empty
-- 3. Create preset
-- Expected result: Phosphate becomes visible in library
- [x] Verify all components fully defined become visible monomers
-- 1. Define base, sugar, phosphate fully
-- 2. Create preset
-- Expected result: All three monomers appear as visible items
- [x] Verify hidden monomer is created when required properties are missing
-- 1. Define structure only for a component
-- 2. Leave required fields empty
-- 3. Create preset
-- Expected result: Component saved internally but not shown in library or search
- [x] Verify mixed visibility: base defined, others hidden
-- 1. Define base fully
-- 2. Leave sugar and phosphate undefined
-- 3. Create preset
-- 4. Open monomer library
-- Expected result: Only base is visible; sugar/phosphate exist internally but hidden
- [x] Verify uniqueness rules ignore hidden monomers
-- 1. Create preset with hidden base (auto code abcB)
-- 2. Create visible base manually with same code abcB
-- Expected result: No duplicate-code error; visible monomer saved successfully
- [x] Verify hidden monomer auto-assigned type matches component type
-- 1. Create hidden base
-- 2. Export or inspect value
-- Expected result: Type = base (likewise sugar= sugar, phosphate= phosphate)
- [x] Verify auto-assigned code/name for hidden base
-- 1. Create preset with code abc
-- 2. Leave base undefined
-- 3. Create preset
-- Expected result: Hidden base receives code abcB and name abcB
- [x] Verify auto-assigned code/name for hidden sugar
-- 1. Create preset with code abc
-- 2. Leave sugar undefined
-- 3. Create preset
-- Expected result: Sugar receives code abcS and name abcS
- [x] Verify auto-assigned code/name for hidden phosphate
-- 1. Create preset with code abc
-- 2. Leave phosphate undefined
-- 3. Create preset
-- Expected result: Phosphate receives code abcP and name abcP
- [x] Verify natural analogue auto-assigned to hidden base
-- 1. Create hidden base
-- 2. Inspect natural analogue
-- Expected result: Value = X
- [x] Verify correct structure assignment to hidden monomer
-- 1. Assign structure fragment to base/sugar/phosphate
-- 2. Create preset
-- 3. Inspect hidden monomer structure
-- Expected result: Structure matches selected fragment
- [x] Verify AP Scenario 1.1: phosphate→base→sugar
-- 1. Assign phosphate
-- 2. Assign base
-- 3. Assign sugar
-- 4. Inspect APs
-- Expected result: APs match expected final sugar-base-phosphate layout
- [x] Verify AP Scenario 1.2: base→phosphate→sugar
-- 1. Assign base
-- 2. Assign phosphate
-- 3. Assign sugar
-- Expected result: Same AP layout as Scenario 1.1
- [x] Verify AP Scenario 1.3: phosphate→sugar→base
-- 1. Assign phosphate
-- 2. Assign sugar
-- 3. Assign base
-- Expected result: Correct AP mapping for this order
- [x] Verify AP Scenario 1.4: base→sugar→phosphate
-- 1. Assign base
-- 2. Assign sugar
-- 3. Assign phosphate
-- Expected result: Equivalent result to Scenario 1.3
- [x] Verify AP Scenario 1.5: sugar→phosphate→base with AP flipping
-- 1. Assign sugar first
-- 2. Assign phosphate second
-- 3. Validate if AP flip is required
-- 4. Assign base
-- Expected result: Sugar AP flips if connection does not match expected R2/H–R1/OH
- [x] Verify AP Scenario 1.6: sugar→base→phosphate with flipping if needed
-- 1. Assign sugar first
-- 2. Assign base second
-- 3. Assign phosphate
-- 4. Inspect AP
-- Expected result: Sugar AP flips if sugar–base connectivity mismatches expected rules
- [x] Verify AP Scenario 2.1: phosphate→sugar
-- 1. Assign phosphate
-- 2. Assign sugar
-- 3. Inspect AP
-- Expected result: Correct sugar–phosphate AP assignment
- [x] Verify AP Scenario 2.2: sugar→phosphate
-- 1. Assign sugar first
-- 2. Assign phosphate
-- 3. Inspect AP
-- Expected result: No AP flip required; APs correct
- [x] Verify AP Scenario 3.1: base→sugar
-- 1. Assign base
-- 2. Assign sugar
-- 3. Inspect AP
-- Expected result: Correct sugar-base AP assignment
- [x] Verify AP Scenario 3.2: sugar→base with AP flipping
-- 1. Assign sugar first
-- 2. Assign base
-- 3. Inspect AP
-- Expected result: Sugar AP is flipped to satisfy expected connection
- [x] Integration: verify preset works in RNA/DNA builder
-- 1. Create preset
-- 2. Build chain
-- 3. Inspect generated structure
-- Expected result: Chain builds successfully with correct bonding and AP behavior
- [x] Integration: verify export/import preserves monomer data
-- 1. Build chain using preset
-- 2. Export structure
-- 3. Import structure
-- 4. Inspect monomers/APs
-- Expected result: Data preserved; hidden/visible monomers remain correct
- [x] Regression: verify manual monomer creation still works
-- 1. Create standalone monomer via library
-- 2. Fill properties
-- 3. Save monomer
-- Expected result: Behavior unchanged; uniqueness validation works normally

entries.title: Autotests: Defining the monomer structure - presets in the monomer creation wizard
entries.body:
**Source task(s):**
 - https://github.com/epam/ketcher/issues/8850

- [x] Verify 'Mark as a...' context menu option is available for Nucleotide (preset) with continuous selection
-- 1. Open Monomer Creation Wizard
-- 2. Set monomer type to 'Nucleotide (preset)'
-- 3. On the canvas inside the wizard, select a continuous fragment intended as a preset component
-- 4. Right-click on the selection to open the context menu
-- Expected result: 'Mark as a...' option is visible and enabled in the context menu for a continuous selection when type is 'Nucleotide (preset)'	
- [x] Verify 'Mark as a...' is not visible for non-preset monomer types
-- 1. Open Monomer Creation Wizard
-- 2. Set monomer type to a type other than 'Nucleotide (preset)' (e.g., 'Small molecule' or 'Nucleotide (monomer)')
-- 3. Select any continuous fragment on the canvas
-- 4. Right-click on the selection to open the context menu
-- Expected result: Context menu does NOT contain the 'Mark as a...' option for non-preset monomer types	
- [x] Verify 'Mark as a...' context menu has Base, Sugar, and Phosphate sub-options
-- 1. Open Monomer Creation Wizard
-- 2. Set monomer type to 'Nucleotide (preset)'
-- 3. Select a continuous fragment
-- 4. Right-click to open context menu
-- 5. Hover over 'Mark as a...' entry
-- Expected result: A submenu appears under 'Mark as a...' with three options labeled exactly: 'Base', 'Sugar', and 'Phosphate'	
- [x] Verify 'Mark as a...' is disabled for non-continuous selection
-- 1. Open Monomer Creation Wizard
-- 2. Set monomer type to 'Nucleotide (preset)'
-- 3. Select two or more non-connected fragments (non-continuous selection)
-- 4. Right-click to open context menu
-- Expected result: 'Mark as a...' entry is present but disabled (greyed out / not clickable) for non-continuous selection	
- [x] Verify 'Mark as a...' becomes enabled when switching back to continuous selection
-- 1. From previous test, clear the non-continuous selection
-- 2. Select a single continuous fragment
-- 3. Right-click to open context menu
-- Expected result: 'Mark as a...' entry becomes enabled again once the selection is continuous	
- [x] Verify marking a fragment as Base via context menu opens Base tab and assigns structure
-- 1. Open Monomer Creation Wizard
-- 2. Set monomer type to 'Nucleotide (preset)'
-- 3. Select a continuous fragment that should serve as Base
-- 4. Right-click and choose 'Mark as a... > Base'
-- 5. Observe wizard tabs and Base component section
-- Expected result: Base tab (or Base section) becomes active/open; selected fragment is assigned as the Base structure for the preset component	
- [x] Verify marking a fragment as Sugar via context menu opens Sugar tab and assigns structure
-- 1. Open Monomer Creation Wizard
-- 2. Set monomer type to 'Nucleotide (preset)'
-- 3. Select a continuous fragment that should serve as Sugar
-- 4. Right-click and choose 'Mark as a... > Sugar'
-- 5. Observe wizard tabs and Sugar component section
-- Expected result: Sugar tab (or Sugar section) becomes active/open; selected fragment is assigned as the Sugar structure for the preset component	
- [x] Verify marking a fragment as Phosphate via context menu opens Phosphate tab and assigns structure
-- 1. Open Monomer Creation Wizard
-- 2. Set monomer type to 'Nucleotide (preset)'
-- 3. Select a continuous fragment that should serve as Phosphate
-- 4. Right-click and choose 'Mark as a... > Phosphate'
-- 5. Observe wizard tabs and Phosphate component section
-- Expected result: Phosphate tab (or Phosphate section) becomes active/open; selected fragment is assigned as the Phosphate structure for the preset component	
- [x] Verify user can set component structure using dedicated button in Attributes panel for continuous selection
-- 1. Open Monomer Creation Wizard
-- 2. Set monomer type to 'Nucleotide (preset)'
-- 3. Select a continuous fragment on canvas
-- 4. In the Attributes panel, locate dedicated control/button to mark selection as Base/Sugar/Phosphate
-- 5. Click the appropriate button (e.g., 'Set as Base')
-- Expected result: Selected fragment is assigned to the chosen component (Base/Sugar/Phosphate), and the corresponding component tab/section reflects the structure	
- [x] Verify dedicated Attributes panel button is disabled for non-continuous selection
-- 1. Open Monomer Creation Wizard
-- 2. Set monomer type to 'Nucleotide (preset)'
-- 3. Select non-continuous fragments on the canvas
-- 4. Observe the dedicated mark-as-component controls in the Attributes panel
-- Expected result: Controls/buttons that assign selection as Base/Sugar/Phosphate are disabled and cannot be used when the selection is non-continuous	
- [x] Verify multiple components can be defined sequentially using 'Mark as a...' on different selections
-- 1. Open Monomer Creation Wizard and set type to 'Nucleotide (preset)'
-- 2. Select continuous fragment for Base and mark 'Mark as a... > Base'
-- 3. Select a different continuous fragment for Sugar and mark 'Mark as a... > Sugar'
-- 4. Select a third continuous fragment for Phosphate and mark 'Mark as a... > Phosphate'
-- 5. Inspect all three component tabs/sections
-- Expected result: Base, Sugar, and Phosphate tabs/sections each contain their respective assigned structures; previous assignments are preserved and not overwritten unexpectedly

entries.title: Autotests: Additions to the structure - presets in the monomer creation wizard
entries.body:
**Source task(s):**
 - https://github.com/epam/ketcher/issues/8852

- [x] Verify that additions connected to Base become part of Base component
-- 1. Open Monomer Creation Wizard and select 'Nucleotide (preset)'.
-- 2. Define initial preset components (Base, Sugar, Phosphate) using the wizard so that each has a marked structure.
-- 3. On the canvas, draw a new atom/bond directly attached to the existing Base structure (e.g., extend a chain from Base or add a substituent to Base).
-- 4. Open the Base component section in the wizard and inspect its assigned structure.
-- Expected result: The newly drawn atoms/bonds that are directly connected to the Base structure are included in the Base component structure; Sugar and Phosphate components remain unchanged.
- [x] Verify that additions connected to Sugar become part of Sugar component
-- 1. With Base, Sugar, and Phosphate already defined in the preset wizard, select the Sugar structure on the canvas.
-- 2. Draw a new atom or substituent attached to the Sugar (e.g., add a sulfur to the OH group of the sugar as in the example from the ticket).
-- 3. Open the Sugar component section and inspect its structure.
-- Expected result: The new addition (e.g., sulfur) is part of the Sugar component structure; Base and Phosphate structures are not modified.
- [x] Verify that additions connected to Phosphate become part of Phosphate component
-- 1. With all three components already defined, select the Phosphate structure on the canvas.
-- 2. Draw new atoms/bonds directly attached to the Phosphate (e.g., extend the phosphate chain).
-- 3. Open the Phosphate component section and inspect its structure.
-- Expected result: All newly drawn atoms/bonds attached to Phosphate are included in the Phosphate component structure only; Base and Sugar components are unchanged.
- [x] Verify that unconnected additions do not belong to any component and block preset saving
-- 1. Ensure Base, Sugar, and Phosphate are already defined for the preset.
-- 2. On the canvas, draw a new structure that is completely unconnected to any of the existing components (e.g., an isolated cyclohexane ring).
-- 3. Attempt to save the preset via the wizard.
-- 4. Observe system behavior and error feedback.
-- Expected result: The unconnected structure is not assigned to Base, Sugar, or Phosphate. Saving the preset fails with an error (as per req. 4.1.1 in another ticket) indicating that there is structure on the canvas not belonging to any component.
- [x] Verify that previously unconnected structure becomes part of Base when connected to Base
-- 1. Start from the scenario with an unconnected structure (e.g., cyclohexane) on the canvas and assigned Base, Sugar, and Phosphate components.
-- 2. Connect the unconnected structure to the Base by adding bonds (e.g., through an amino group on the Base), so the new structure is now directly connected only to Base.
-- 3. Open the Base component section in the wizard.
-- 4. Attempt to save the preset.
-- Expected result: The previously unconnected structure is now part of the Base component structure. Preset save is allowed with no errors related to unassigned structures.
- [x] Verify that previously unconnected structure becomes part of another single component when connected (Sugar or Phosphate)
-- 1. Create an unconnected structure on the canvas with defined Base, Sugar, and Phosphate components.
-- 2. Connect this structure only to the Sugar component (e.g., via a bond to a Sugar atom).
-- 3. Inspect the Sugar component structure.
-- 4. Attempt to save the preset.
-- Expected result: The previously unconnected structure becomes part of the Sugar component. Preset can be saved successfully without unassigned-structure errors.
- [x] Verify behavior when structure connected to one component is subsequently extended to another component (multi-component connection)
-- 1. Start from the case where a previously unconnected structure has been connected to Base and is now part of Base.
-- 2. Draw additional bonds from this structure so that it also connects to Sugar (resulting in a fragment connecting Base and Sugar, as in the ticket example).
-- 3. Inspect which component the connecting fragment belongs to in the wizard.
-- 4. Attempt to save the preset.
-- Expected result: The connecting structure retains its original component marking (it remains part of Base, per ticket). Saving the preset fails with an error related to component connectivity (per req. 4.3.1 in another ticket) because the same marked structure is connected to more than one component.
- [x] Verify behavior when part of a component structure is disconnected and reconnected to another component
-- 1. With Base, Sugar, and Phosphate defined, select a portion of the Base structure that is clearly part of Base.
-- 2. Break bonds to detach this portion from the rest of the Base so that the Base component becomes non-continuous.
-- 3. Connect the detached portion to another component (e.g., to Sugar) by adding bonds.
-- 4. Inspect markings for that detached portion in the wizard.
-- 5. Attempt to save the preset.
-- Expected result: The detached and reconnected portion retains its original component marking (it is still considered part of Base, not reassigned to Sugar). Preset saving fails, producing an error for multi-component connectivity (req. 4.3.1) and an error for non-continuous monomer structure. Component markings are not automatically changed to avoid the 'ship of Theseus' problem."
- [x] Verify that adding and removing simple extensions to a component does not break component continuity
-- 1. With Base, Sugar, and Phosphate defined, extend one of the components (e.g., Base) by adding a short side chain.
-- 2. Confirm the side chain is part of the component.
-- 3. Delete the added atoms/bonds (undo or erase).
-- 4. Inspect the component structure for continuity and correctness.
-- 5. Attempt to save the preset.
-- Expected result: After adding then removing simple extensions, the component structure remains valid and continuous. Preset saves successfully, and there are no residual unassigned fragments or continuity errors.
- [x] Verify that additions made before components are defined are handled correctly once components are defined
-- 1. In the wizard, before marking any component, draw several fragments on the canvas (some connected, some unconnected).
-- 2. Then define Base, Sugar, and Phosphate components by marking appropriate continuous fragments.
-- 3. Inspect which parts of the pre-existing structures got assigned to which components.
-- 4. Attempt to save the preset when some remaining fragments are not assigned to any component.
-- Expected result: Fragments explicitly used for Base, Sugar, and Phosphate become part of their respective components. Any leftover fragments that do not belong to a component prevent preset saving, producing an error about extraneous unassigned structure (per req. 4.1.1 in another ticket).

entries.title: Autotests: Only show the possible monomer properties in the attributes panel in the monomer creation wizard
entries.body:
**Source task(s):**
 - https://github.com/epam/ketcher/issues/8778

- [x] Verify attributes panel sections for CHEM monomer type match allowed properties table
-- 1. Open Monomer Creation Wizard.
-- 2. In the monomer type dropdown, select 'CHEM'.
-- 3. Open the Attributes panel.
-- 4. Inspect the presence of fields/sections: Name, Code, Natural analogue, Modification, Aliases (HELM/IDT/AxoLabs), Attachment points.
-- Expected result: For type 'CHEM':
-- - Name and Code fields are present.
-- - Natural analogue field is NOT shown.
-- - 'Modification' section is NOT shown.
-- - 'Aliases' section IS shown because CHEM supports aliases (IDT and AxoLabs). Only the implemented alias fields are displayed (HELM alias is not present as CHEM cannot have HELM alias).
-- - 'Attachment points' section is present.
No other monomer-specific property sections outside the table row are shown.
- [x] Verify attributes panel sections for Amino acid monomer type match allowed properties table
-- 1. Open Monomer Creation Wizard.
-- 2. In the monomer type dropdown, select 'Amino acid'.
-- 3. Open the Attributes panel.
-- 4. Inspect the presence of fields/sections: Name, Code, Natural analogue, Modification, Aliases, Attachment points.
-- Expected result: For type 'Amino acid':
-- - Name, Code, and Natural analogue fields are present.
-- - 'Modification' section IS present (amino acids support modification type).
-- - 'Aliases' section IS present and contains HELM alias field; IDT and AxoLabs alias inputs are NOT shown (type does not support them).
-- - 'Attachment points' section is present.
-- Properties that are marked as not available in the table are not shown in the Attributes panel."
- [x] Verify attributes panel sections for Sugar monomer type match allowed properties tabl
-- 1. Open Monomer Creation Wizard.
-- 2. In the monomer type dropdown, select 'Sugar'.
-- 3. Open the Attributes panel.
-- 4. Inspect the presence of fields/sections: Name, Code, Natural analogue, Modification, Aliases, Attachment points.
-- Expected result: For type 'Sugar':
-- - Name and Code fields are present.
-- - Natural analogue field is NOT shown.
-- - 'Modification' section is NOT shown (sugars cannot have modification type).
-- - 'Aliases' section IS present and only HELM alias is available; IDT and AxoLabs alias fields are not shown.
-- - 'Attachment points' section is present.
-- No additional monomer property sections are displayed beyond those allowed in the table.
- [x] Verify attributes panel sections for Base monomer type match allowed properties table
-- 1. Open Monomer Creation Wizard.
-- 2. In the monomer type dropdown, select 'Base'.
-- 3. Open the Attributes panel.
-- 4. Inspect the presence of fields/sections: Name, Code, Natural analogue, Modification, Aliases, Attachment points.
-- Expected result: For type 'Base':
-- - Name, Code, and Natural analogue fields are present.
-- - 'Modification' section is NOT shown.
-- - 'Aliases' section IS present and contains HELM alias only; IDT and AxoLabs alias fields are not shown.
-- - 'Attachment points' section is present.
-- No properties absent in the table (e.g., modification type) appear in the UI.
- [x] Verify attributes panel sections for Phosphate monomer type match allowed properties table
-- 1. Open Monomer Creation Wizard.
-- 2. In the monomer type dropdown, select 'Phosphate'.
-- 3. Open the Attributes panel.
-- 4. Inspect the presence of fields/sections: Name, Code, Natural analogue, Modification, Aliases, Attachment points.
-- Expected result: For type 'Phosphate':
-- - Name and Code fields are present.
-- - Natural analogue field is NOT shown.
-- - 'Modification' section is NOT shown.
-- - 'Aliases' section IS present and supports HELM alias and (where implemented) IDT and AxoLabs aliases per table.
-- - 'Attachment points' section is present.
-- No additional monomer properties beyond those allowed in the table are visible.
- [x] Verify attributes panel sections for 'Nucleotide (monomer)' type match allowed properties table
-- 1. Open Monomer Creation Wizard.
-- 2. In the monomer type dropdown, select 'Nucleotide (monomer)'.
-- 3. Open the Attributes panel.
-- 4. Inspect the presence of fields/sections: Name, Code, Natural analogue, Modification, Aliases, Attachment points.
-- Expected result: For type 'Nucleotide (monomer)':
-- - Name, Code, and Natural analogue fields are present.
-- - 'Modification' section is NOT shown (the table marks modification type as not available).
-- - 'Aliases' section IS present, but only IDT and AxoLabs alias fields are shown; HELM alias is not present.
-- - 'Attachment points' section is present.
-- The Attributes panel shows only the monomer properties allowed by the table.
- [x] Verify preset-level attributes panel for 'Nucleotide (preset)' only shows preset-specific properties
-- 1. Open Monomer Creation Wizard.
-- 2. In the monomer type dropdown, select 'Nucleotide (preset)'.
-- 3. Open the Attributes panel for the preset itself (not for individual components).
-- 4. Inspect which fields/sections are available (e.g. preset Name/Code, aliases, attachment-related properties).
-- Expected result: For type 'Nucleotide (preset)':
-- - The Attributes panel shows only properties that apply to the preset as a whole according to the table (e.g., preset-level Code and any allowed aliases or attachment-related properties).
-- - Properties that belong to component monomers (e.g., component modification type, component natural analogue) are NOT shown at the preset level.
-- - A note from the ticket is respected: components (Base/Sugar/Phosphate) have the same monomer properties as when created as standalone monomers, but those are edited in their own context, not as preset-level attributes.
- [x] Verify that changing monomer type dynamically updates visible sections in the attributes panel according to the table
-- 1. Open Monomer Creation Wizard.
-- 2. Select 'Amino acid' as monomer type and open the Attributes panel; note that 'Modification' and HELM alias fields are visible.
-- 3. Without closing the wizard, change the monomer type to 'Sugar'.
-- 4. Observe the Attributes panel again.
-- 5. Change type to 'CHEM' and inspect once more.
-- Expected result: When switching type:
-- - After selecting 'Amino acid', the Attributes panel shows 'Modification' and HELM alias (and hides unsupported alias fields).
-- - After switching to 'Sugar', the 'Modification' section disappears, HELM alias remains, and other unsupported alias fields stay hidden.
-- - After switching to 'CHEM', HELM alias disappears, while aliases for IDT/AxoLabs become available and the 'Modification' section remains hidden.
-- At each step, the visible sections match exactly the configuration from the requirements table.
- [x] Verify that 'Aliases' section is hidden when no alias types are allowed for a monomer type
-- 1. Identify or create (in configuration/fixtures) a monomer type for which the table specifies no HELM, IDT, or AxoLabs aliases (all three columns are 'X').
-- 2. Open Monomer Creation Wizard.
-- 3. Select this monomer type in the type dropdown.
-- 4. Open the Attributes panel and inspect whether an 'Aliases' section is present.
-- Expected result: For any monomer type where the table has all alias columns (HELM, IDT, AxoLabs) marked as not available:
-- - The 'Aliases' section is completely absent from the Attributes panel.
-- This confirms the rule: if a monomer type cannot have IDT, AxoLabs, or HELM aliases, the Aliases section must be hidden."
